sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the 
 testing procedures P1, which must be performed on a daily 
 basis as indicated by D1 in the above title block, and according to the 
 Directives of the Central Chemical Laboratories.

This 
Practice covers the sampling of water for chemical and physical analysis.

The following is included : 
Practice A - Grab Samples
Significance

The goal of sampling is to 
obtain a truly representative sample.

The most critical factors 
necessary to achieve this are :
Points of sampling.
Time of sampling.
Frequency of sampling.

sections.text: Summary of Practices

This practice includes Grab Samples 
procedure which is applicable to sample water at a specific site representing conditions only at the 
time of sampling from sources such as wells, rivers, streams, pipe lines and steam generators.
Definitions

Sampling- obtaining of a portion 
representative of the material concerned to be analysed.

Safety 
Precautions

The sample must be taken as the applicable ASTM methods D 
 3370-76.
Make sure the sample bottle is correctly labeled.
Make sure the sample bottle is free from dust and dirt.

The sample must be kept away from exposure to direct 
 sunlight.

Cleaning solvents such as acid 
 dichromate, nitric acid and others are 
 dangerous, so 
 you have to wear breathing mask.

Keep 
 this solvents closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do 
 not breathe them, use only in a hood.

sections.text: Tools and Equipments

Reagents 
 and Materials
Purity of Reagents

All reagents shall conform to the specifications of the 
committee on Analytical Reagents of the American Chemical Society, where such 
specifications are available. Other grades may be used, provided that the 
reagent is of high purity to permit its use without lessening the accuracy of 
the determination.
Cleaning Solutions

1. Acid Dichromate ( 32 g / 1 Litre H2SO4, 
sp.gr 1.84 ).

2. Nitric Acid ( 1 v HNO3 /4 
v H2O, sp.gr 1.42 ).

3. Sodium Thiosulfate ( Na2S2O3 
), powdered.
Work to be carried out

Frequency and 
 Duration of Sampling

If samples of water are taken far 
 enough from the shoreline it may be made by taking individual samples at 
 infrequent intervals, such as bi- weekly or monthly, sufficient to cover 
 seasonal changes.

If samples of water are taken near 
 from the shoreline of river, take them at shorterintervals, for instance daily

to provide more exact knowledge of 
 the variation in composition where these are of importance in the use to which 
 the water is to be put.

If greater variation or cycles of 
 pollution occur collect more frequent samples, for example, at hourly 
 intervals.

Water undergoing continuous 
 treatment must be sampled with such frequency that adequate control is 
 assured.

The interval between samples is 
 directly related to the rate at which critical characteristics can reach 
 intolerable limits.

Temperature 
 Adjustment

When 
 samples above ambient temperature are taken, use cooling coils for adjusting 
 it to the ambient temperature. Some test methods require adjustment to other 
 than ambient temperature and can be carried out when indicated.

Particulate 
 Matter
Normally, samples are taken without separation of particulate matter.

 Sample

Preparation 
 of Sample Containers for Chemical and Physical Analysis

The 
 sample containers shall be made of materials that will not contaminate with 
 the sample and before use shall be cleaned thoroughly to remove all extraneous 
 surface dirt. Chemically resistant glass and polyethylene are suitable 
 materials for the containers. The closures for it shall be glass stoppers that 
 have been thoroughly washed, or plastic caps with suitable liners.

Point of 
 Sampling

Open Bodies 
 of Water

Choose 
 it with extreme care to obtain a representative sample of water, avoid surface 
 scum.

For 
 streams, seas, reservoirs, and other bodies of water, samples are taken at a 
 number of points at the surface and at a number of depths at each points.

The 
 distance between samples is from 1 to 3 miles below the source of pollution.

Collect samples at least one- half mile below water falls to obtain time for 
 escaping entrained air.

sections.text:
Confined 
 Flows

Choose 
 sampling points in pipelines, filters, zeolite and chemical water softeners, 
 deionizing processes, surface condensers, evaporators or condensate return 
 lines with regard to the piping and 
 configuration of the individual piece of equipment containing the water to be 
 tested, the 
 character and changes occurring between the inlet and outlet water, and the 
 rate of passage through the equipment.

Steam 
 Generators

The exact point of sampling depends on : 
steam generator design, location of chemical and

water feed, lines, and other local conditions. Samples taken from several 
locations

simultaneously may be desirable. 
Collect samples through a cooling coil.

Sample 
 Collection for Chemical and 
 Physical Analysis

items:
To 
 sample streams under pressure, regulate the rate of flow in the sample line 
 to not less than 500 ml / min. after first flushing to remove all sediment 
 and gas pockets. Samples at elevated temperature must be collected through a 
 cooling coil.

To 
 sample water from valves or cocks, insert the sample line into the sampling 
 bottle so that it touches the bottom. Allow a volume of water to flow into 
 and overflow from the container before the sample is taken. Fill the 
 container completely and secure the sample without contact with air to 
 prevent change in the concentration of constituent to be determined.

To 
 sample unconfined water at any specific depth flows samples through a tube 
 to the bottom of the container and a volume of sample equal to 4 to 10 times 
 the volume of the container passes through it, or an integrated sample 
 containing water from all points in a vertical section.

To 
 sample water from steam generator, take precautions to avoid dilution by 
 condensed steam or concentration due to flashing.

To 
 ship samples, do not fill the bottle entirely in order to allow some room 
 for expansion when subjected to a change in temperature. An air space of 10 
 to 25 ml usually sufficient.

Before taking the sample, establish a continuous flow of not less than 500 
 ml / min., cooled to less than 37C and also rinse the sample container at 
 least 3 times by filling it with water to be sampled, shaking, then 
 emptying.

Collect the water sample by upward displacement through a tube extending to 
 the bottom of container. Allow it to overflow at least 5 times, then stopper 
 it. If analysis can not be made immediately, the containers should be 
 tightly stoppered to prevent atmospheric contamination.

sections.text: Preservation of Sample

Add 
 chemical preservations to samples for chemical and physical examinations 
 only as specified in specific test methods. Quick freezing has been found to 
 be beneficial in preserving some organic constituents.

Time Interval 
 Between Collection and Analysis of Samples

In 
 general, allow as short a time as possible to elapse between the collection 
 of a sample and its analysis. Under some conditions, analysis is necessary 
 to secure reliable results.
Labeling and transportation of Sample

1. Provide space for the following 
 information on an etched area of the bottle, a cardboard securely affixed to 
 the container.
sample number,
date and time of sampling,
source of sample,

2. The 
 sample shipping containers shall be hold in place with spring clips, 
 sawdust, excelsior, foamed plastic.

3. Use insulated containers for quick frozen 
samples usually shipped with solid

carbon dioxide to maintain the 
sample in frozen condition.
